items.requirement: The API suite runs only after an application endpoint is available.
The API suite reads a project-owned declarative test file.
HTTP, API flow, and OpenAPI checks are separate provider nodes.
The test file supports shared values used by later requests.
The test file supports setup requests.
The test file supports cleanup requests.
Request methods, paths, headers, and bodies are explicit.
Unknown flow fields and assertions are rejected before network access.
Flow files use the version kubeclaw.api-flow.v1.
The suite performs real HTTP requests.
The suite performs real WebSocket exchanges.
Request timeouts fail the affected step.
Operator policy limits origins, ports, methods, headers, request bytes, response bytes, and time.
Redirects cannot escape the approved target.
Status assertions are strict.
Content-type assertions are strict.
Response text assertions are strict.
JSON selector assertions are strict.
WebSocket message assertions are strict.
Setup output can be extracted into a variable.
Only a step that references a missing output is skipped.
Cleanup runs after failed main requests.
OpenAPI operations are selected by operation ID or tag.
OpenAPI never runs every operation implicitly.
Requests are checked against declared parameters and request schemas before sending.
Responses are checked for status, content type, schema, and required headers.
Each provider writes bounded structured evidence.
Response secrets and bodies do not enter the provider summary.
A numeric failure allowance could hide failed assertions.
An informational default could report success after failures.
Network mutation authority was not expressed as operator policy.
The legacy API runner and protocol selection are absent after cutover.
